overnight.summary: Barclays cuts Netflix price target to $65 while keeping an equal-weight rating.
Analysts keep positive ratings on Netflix but cut price targets to $78‑$80, indicating modest downside pressure.
Bernstein keeps an Outperform rating on Netflix but cuts its price target to $80, indicating modest concerns.
Netflix shares fell to a 52‑week low after weak Q4 guidance despite a Q3 earnings beat.
Analyst downgrades include Netflix, adding to the negative sentiment around the stock.
Netflix fell ~6-7% pre‑market after mixed Q3 results and weaker-than‑expected guidance.
Rosenblatt keeps a neutral rating on Netflix and cuts its price target to $71.
Roku faces a patent infringement lawsuit filed by VB Assets LLC in Delaware federal court.
Morgan Stanley cut its price target for Netflix to $77, indicating a more bearish outlook.
Needham downgrades Netflix to Hold, suggesting weaker outlook
Morgan Stanley keeps overweight rating but cuts price target to $77, indicating modest concerns
BofA Securities maintains a buy rating on Netflix but cuts its price target to $90, indicating modest concerns about growth.
CFO projects double‑digit revenue growth through 2027 despite modest viewership gains, citing diversified content and stable growth drivers.
CEO warns competition from YouTube and TikTok, pledges higher‑quality shows and movies to retain viewers.
CFO says view‑hour growth is lagging, but upcoming Brad Pitt, Narnia and NFL content are expected to boost engagement.
Disney is mentioned only in passing and faces no new material news.
Chamath Palihapitiya criticized Netflix’s content strategy and rising debt, and shares fell after weak guidance.
